dataset.name: Scogo Sovereign Enterprise NetOps — Prompt Seeds, Part 1
dataset.description: 3,500 synthetic enterprise network-operations task prompts (prompt seeds) sampled from the compositional taxonomy `scogo-enterprise-netops-v2`. Each record is a self-contained, fictional operational scenario — an incident ticket, on-call chat, CLI session, config review, change request, war room, audit, architecture review, or automation brief — carrying embedded evidence fixtures (configs, logs, telemetry, packet summaries, routing tables, topology) and a task instruction. Records are PROMPTS ONLY: there are no reference answers, no assistant messages, no tool results, and no ground-truth labels.
dataset.intended_use: Seed corpus for teacher-trajectory generation, model evaluation on enterprise NetOps reasoning, and rubric/judge development. This is stage 1 of the pipeline defined in docs/netops-data-contract.md; a schema-valid, review-accepted prompt is not a verified or trainable trajectory.
dataset.out_of_scope: Telecom / service-provider network operations (3GPP RAN, EPC, 5GC, IMS, spectrum planning, carrier OSS/BSS, carrier optical backbone) and certification-exam question generation are excluded by the taxonomy scope.

file.format: JSON Lines (one JSON object per line, UTF-8, LF line endings, trailing newline)
file.note_non_ascii: 21 distinct non-ASCII codepoints, all typographic: em/en dashes (U+2014, U+2013), curly quotes (U+2019, U+201C, U+201D), arrows (U+2192, U+2194, U+2190), and a few math/unit symbols (≤ ≥ × ± µ ° −). No CJK, no emoji. Normalize if a downstream tokenizer or store requires ASCII.

prompt.description: The full task text handed to a model. Self-contained: scenario framing, embedded evidence fixtures, and the instruction.

category.description: Top-level taxonomy category. Constant `enterprise_netops` in this part.

domain.description: Networking domain, e.g. layer3_routing, firewall_network_security. 25 values present.

subdomain.description: Specific technical topic within the domain, e.g. bgp_route_leak. 517 distinct values present.

difficulty.description: Sampled difficulty. Bounded per task_family by the taxonomy.

coordinates.description: The compositional taxonomy coordinate the prompt was generated to realize. See coordinates_fields.

taskgen_model.description: Model that authored the prompt text.

language.description: Optional in the schema; ABSENT from every record in this file.

coordinates_fields.taxonomy_id: Taxonomy that defines the axes. Constant `scogo-enterprise-netops-v2`.
coordinates_fields.category_id: Mirrors the top-level `category`. Verified equal in all 3,500 records.
coordinates_fields.task_family: What kind of work the task demands (RCA, telemetry interpretation, config review, next-best-action, change/rollback, abstention, architecture).
coordinates_fields.environment: Where the scenario sits (campus, branch, data_center, hybrid, cloud, multicloud, kubernetes, remote_access, enterprise_wireless, ot, ai_hpc, edge, lab_staging).
coordinates_fields.platform_scope: Enum: platform_neutral | single_platform | multi_platform. Constrains `platforms` cardinality to 0, 1, and 2 respectively.
coordinates_fields.platforms: Array of vendor/platform ids, unique. Empty for platform_neutral.
coordinates_fields.incident_mechanism: The underlying fault class the scenario encodes.
coordinates_fields.evidence_condition: Quality of the supplied evidence: sufficient | partial | contradictory | stale | missing_live_state. Non-`sufficient` values are deliberate — they test abstention and escalation.
coordinates_fields.evidence_bundle: Which artifact types are embedded in the prompt.
coordinates_fields.action_risk: How much action the task authorizes: read_only_investigation | advisory_plan_only | approval_gated_change | staging_or_simulation | emergency_change_decision.
coordinates_fields.presentation: Surface form / channel the prompt is written as.

validation.method: Field-by-field check of every record against schemas/task-v2.schema.json (required keys, no additional properties, types, enums, ranges, platform_scope/platforms cardinality, platforms uniqueness, category_id == category).
validation.note_coordinate_uniqueness: All 3,500 coordinate tuples (domain, subdomain, task_family, environment, incident_mechanism, evidence_condition, evidence_bundle, action_risk, presentation, platform_scope, platforms) are distinct — no coordinate is realized twice.
validation.note_difficulty_bounds: Every record's difficulty falls inside the per-task_family difficulty_min/difficulty_max declared in docs/netops-taxonomy.yaml. Zero violations.

in_pipeline.scope: Applied within each generation run against that run's accumulated corpus.

post_merge_check.lexical_near_duplicate_scan: 5-gram Jaccard over all within-domain pairs (297,813 pairs)
post_merge_check.caveat: The post-merge scan is lexical only and restricted to within-domain pairs. A cross-lineage semantic (embedding) dedup pass between the 3,000-record chain and the 500-record run was not run. Lexical overlap is negligible, so semantic near-duplicates are unlikely but not proven absent.

removed_during_merge.reason: The netops-deepseek-qwen38-max-resume2 output (1,000 records) is a strict byte-for-byte subset of netops-deepseek-qwen38-max-2000-resume (3,000 records) — the latter resumed from the former. Those 1,000 records were kept once.

quality_gate.outcomes: accept | revise | reject | needs_verification. Only `accept` records reach this file.
quality_gate.caveat: Reviewer differs across lineages: the 3,000-record chain was reviewed by qwen/qwen3.8-max; the 500-record run was self-reviewed by deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (same model as the generator). The 500 subset therefore carries a weaker, self-review quality signal.

token_cost.note: Sum across the two contributing terminal runs plus the earlier chain runs is not fully reconstructible; figures below are the terminal runs only.

content.nature: Fully synthetic. Every config excerpt, log line, telemetry series, packet summary, hostname, IP, ticket id, and timestamp is a fictional scenario fixture.
content.no_live_access: Prompts must not imply live system access. Embedded evidence is supplied, not fetched.
content.pii: No personal data found. Hostnames, ticket ids, and timestamps are invented. Of 8,523 IPv4 mentions, 8,393 are private/documentation/reserved; the 130 globally-routable ones are well-known public infrastructure used as realistic scenario anchors (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, Azure 168.63.129.16, GCP health-check ranges 35.191.0.0 and 130.211.0.0). 28 email-like strings appear, all on placeholder domains (.local, .example, corp.example.com, contoso.com).

prompt_length.note: No tokenizer was applied. As a rough guide, ~4 chars/token puts the corpus near 2.1M tokens.

content.secrets: Not audited exhaustively. Credential-shaped strings in configs are synthetic scenario fixtures, not live secrets. Do not treat any token in the corpus as valid.

distributions.note: Observed counts over all 3,500 records. Compare against the target weights in docs/netops-taxonomy.yaml.

platforms.note: Counts are mentions, not records: a multi_platform record contributes two.

known_limitations: Single generator model (deepseek-v4-flash-0731) — stylistic and reasoning-pattern homogeneity is expected. No generator diversity in this part.
Mixed reviewer strength: 3,000 records reviewed by an independent model (qwen/qwen3.8-max), 500 self-reviewed by the generator. Treat the 500 as lower-assurance.
Mixed sampling temperature: 2,910 records at 0.4 and 590 at 0.9. The 0.4 majority narrows lexical diversity.
No cross-lineage semantic dedup pass was run after the merge (lexical overlap is negligible; see deduplication.post_merge_check.caveat).

Observed axis distributions drift from taxonomy target weights, mostly because coordinate replacement on rejection reshuffles the sampler. Domains such as cloud_hybrid_networking and firewall_network_security are over-represented relative to weight; enterprise_realtime_networking and packet_protocol_foundations are thin (24 and 34 records).

The 3,000-record terminal run had a 16.6% candidate acceptance rate, driven overwhelmingly by review_error (2,123 of 2,163 rejections) rather than by quality rejections. Those errors are transport/endpoint failures, not judgements about the prompts — but it means the effective review coverage of that wave was retried rather than clean.
Prompts are unlabelled. There is no reference answer, rubric score, or difficulty ground truth to validate the sampled `difficulty` integer against.
No train/validation/test split is defined. If you split, group by domain+subdomain to avoid topical leakage.
Quality was judged by LLM review only. No human review pass has been performed on this part.
